title: The effect of feeding xanthan gum on colonic function in man: correlation with in vitro determinants of bacterial breakdown
authors: Daly J, Tomlin J, Read NW
population: Eighteen healthy male volunteers aged 19 to 34 years, of normal weight for height, without antibiotics in the previous 6 months
funder: not stated. The paper carries no funding or acknowledgement statement; the PubMed record lists no grant support. Author affiliation: Centre for Human Nutrition, University of Sheffield, Northern General Hospital.
inKindSupport: Xanthan gum (Keltrol T) supplied by Kelco International Ltd, San Diego, a xanthan gum manufacturer, in 5 g portions.
result: Xanthan gum 15 g per day, as three 5 g portions in flavoured jelly, was taken for 10 days after a 10-day control period. Stool weight rose from 190.3 (SE 13.6) to 242.8 (15.8) g/day (P < 0.001), stool dry weight from 53.2 to 63.4 g/day (P < 0.008), defaecation frequency from 1.14 to 1.31 per day (P < 0.035) and flatulent episodes from 9.6 to 13.9 per day (P < 0.001); transit time fell from 46.7 to 40.7 hours, not significantly. Before feeding, faecal homogenates from 12 of the 18 men reduced the viscosity of xanthan gum in vitro and 7 abolished it; after 10 days of feeding, 16 of 18 reduced and 11 abolished it, with greater viscosity loss (50.8 against 24.1 mPa.s, P = 0.045) and more hydrogen and short-chain fatty acids (P = 0.049), indicating bacterial adaptation. Reduction in viscosity in vitro did not correlate with the change in stool weight or transit time.
